thread:
Maria: Sales asked for a clear policy: what happens to reserved-pool burst credits if a customer downgrades mid-billing-cycle?
Alex: Two pieces: policy (refund/expiry) + operational rollback if we revoke early.
Jordan: Current system zeros credits on churn which caused C-9032. We need a safer default.
Sam: Ops stance: keep credits until end of cycle, unless there's fraud. That reduces customer surprise.
Priya: Oncall note: if we ever do immediate revoke we must have an automated fallback to avoid traffic drop.
billing-bot: Billing ledger updated in staging: txn-log/v2 now records credit-state transitions.
Maria: Proposal: 1) by default credits valid until cycle end, no prorated refunds; 2) immediate revoke for breach only, requires ops approval and triggers mitigation; 3) prewarm billed as reserved capacity until cycle end and stops on revoke (no refund).
Alex: Mitigation plan for immediate revoke: a) mark pool.expire=true, b) routing-service redirects new requests to fallback model, c) apply soft-throttle (50% for 10m), d) alert PD if error rate >3%.
Jordan: Need audit and customer-visible event for every change. I'll add changelog + billing webhook in the PR.
Sam: I'll prototype routing tag detection and throttle enforcement in staging. Quick patch available.
Priya: I'll write the oncall playbook with explicit rollback steps and test PD alerts in dev.
Maria: Launch criteria: txn logs searchable, routing fallback end-to-end in staging, billing event visible in UI, playbook & owner assigned.
Alex: I'll run staging tests and report back in 48h. :thumbsup:
Maria: If legal needs to approve no-refund language I'll loop them in. Closing actions as assigned above.
